title: Concourse Pipeline
description:
Concourse pipeline.yml

This schema is intended to be used for YAML authoring assistance (Ctrl+Space / Ctrl+Q) in IntelliJ-based IDEs. It focuses on the most common keys and the mental model behind them: resources represent external state, jobs define execution, and plans define steps.

resources.description:
resources: Declares the resources that jobs can interact with.

What it is: A resource is Concourse's abstraction for external state (Git repos, container registries, S3 buckets, notifications, etc.).

How jobs use it:
- get: fetch a version into the build
- put: publish/update a version
- check: detect new versions (usually implicit, configured via check_every / webhooks)

How to configure: Each resource item has at least name, type, and source. The 'source' object is type-specific and forwarded to the resource implementation. Put secrets into ((vars)) instead of hardcoding them.

resource_types.description:
resource_types: Declares custom resource types (resource implementations).

Use this when you need a resource type that isn't built in, or when you want to pin to a specific implementation/version.

Typical shape: the implementation is delivered as a container image (often via base type 'registry-image'); you then reference the resource type by name in resources[].type.

jobs.description:
jobs: Declares the executable units of a pipeline.

A job has a name and a plan (list of steps). It runs when triggered (e.g. trigger: true on a get step, manual trigger, or version constraints via passed).

Use concurrency controls (serial / serial_groups / max_in_flight) to avoid overlapping deployments, and use hooks (on_success/on_failure/ensure) to run cleanup/notifications.

groups.description:
groups: Optional UI-only grouping of jobs in the Concourse dashboard.

This does not affect execution. It only changes how jobs are displayed in the web UI.

var_sources.description:
var_sources: Optional variable sources for resolving ((vars)).

Use this to keep secrets and environment-specific values out of pipeline.yml.

Note: var_sources declares *where* variables come from (Vault, etc.). The variables themselves live in that external system.

display.description:
display: Optional pipeline UI display configuration.

This is Concourse-version dependent and often not required. If you don't know you need it, you can usually omit it.

resource.description:
Resource item.

Required:
- name: referenced by get/put steps
- type: selects the resource implementation
- source: type-specific configuration (credentials/URIs/etc.)

Behavioral knobs:
- check_every: poll interval
- webhook_token: enable webhook-triggered checks (resource-specific)
- tags: worker placement hints

Tip: The content of source depends entirely on the resource type. Concourse treats it as an opaque object.

name.description:
Unique resource name. This is what you reference later using 'get: <name>' or 'put: <name>'.

Best practice: choose stable, descriptive names (e.g. app-repo, image, version, slack).

type.description:
Resource type name.

Built-in examples: git, registry-image.
Custom: if you defined a matching entry in resource_types, use its name here.

This controls which keys the 'source' object supports.

source.description:
Type-specific source configuration object.

Concourse does not interpret the keys inside source. They are passed directly to the resource implementation.

Typical contents: repository URI, branch, credentials, bucket name, region, project IDs, etc.

Security tip: Put secrets into ((vars)) via var_sources/credentials management instead of hardcoding them.

check_every.description:
How often Concourse checks this resource for new versions.

Examples: '10s', '1m', '10m', '1h'.

Lower values = faster detection but higher load on the Concourse scheduler and external systems.

webhook_token.description:
Webhook token for triggering resource checks.

Some resources offer a webhook endpoint so external systems (GitHub/GitLab/etc.) can trigger a check immediately.
This token authenticates the webhook request.

icon.description:
Optional icon name shown in the Concourse UI.

This does not affect execution. It's purely for readability.

public.description:
Expose versions publicly (depends on Concourse auth setup).

Usually safe to omit. Set carefully in multi-tenant environments.

tags.description:
Worker tags for placement.

Concourse may schedule checks/gets/puts on workers that match these tags. Use this for OS/arch constraints or dedicated workers.

resourceType.description:
resource_types item.

A resource type defines a resource implementation (the code that knows how to check/get/put). In practice, resource types are almost always distributed as container images.

When to use resource_types:
- You need a resource type that Concourse doesn't ship with
- You want to pin a specific version of a resource implementation
- You want to use a fork/custom build of a resource

How it connects to resources:
1) Define a resource type here with a unique name
2) Reference it from resources[].type

Required fields:
- name: identifier of the custom type
- type: base type used to fetch/run the implementation (commonly 'registry-image')
- source: configuration to fetch the implementation image (repository/tag/credentials, etc.)

Security tip: Prefer ((vars)) for credentials. Avoid committing secrets into pipeline.yml.

name.description: Unique resource type name. Reference this name from resources[].type.

type.description:
Base resource type used to obtain/run the resource implementation.

Most commonly: registry-image (pull a container image that implements the resource).

source.description:
Type-specific source configuration for fetching the resource implementation image.

Example (registry-image):
- repository: image name
- tag: version tag
- username/password: registry credentials

Concourse forwards this to the base resource type, just like a normal resource source.

privileged.description:
Whether to run this resource type in privileged mode.

Privileged containers have elevated access to the host. Only enable if the resource implementation explicitly requires it.

params.description:
Optional parameters passed to the base resource type when running checks/gets for the resource type itself.

This is base-type-specific. For many setups you can omit it.

Tip: Don’t confuse this with resources[].params for get/put; this params configures the *resource type implementation* container.

check_every.description:
How often Concourse checks for updates of the resource type implementation image.

If you pin a tag (e.g. '1.2.3'), you can set a long interval or omit. If you track 'latest', consider a reasonable interval.

tags.description:
Worker tags for placement when fetching/running the resource type implementation.

Use this if your resource types must run on specific workers (OS/arch, network access, etc.).

group.description:
groups item.

Groups are a Concourse UI feature to organize jobs on the dashboard. They do not change execution semantics.

name.description: Group name displayed in the UI.

jobs.description: List of job names included in this group.

varSource.description:
var_sources item.

Declares an external variable source so Concourse can resolve ((vars)).

Required:
- name: identifier of this source
- type: implementation name (e.g. vault)
- config: connection and configuration (type-specific)

Tip: Prefer injecting secrets through variable sources over hardcoding them in pipeline.yml.

type.description: Variable source type (implementation). Common values depend on Concourse version/installation (e.g. vault, dummy).

config.description: Type-specific config for connecting to the variable source (URL, auth, path prefixes, etc.).

job.description:
jobs item.

A job is executed by Concourse. It consists of a plan (steps).

Recommended minimal keys:
- name
- plan

Concurrency & scheduling:
- serial: never run two builds of this job at the same time
- serial_groups: coordinate concurrency across multiple jobs
- max_in_flight: limit number of concurrent builds

Hooks:
- on_success/on_failure/on_error/ensure: run additional steps based on outcome (notifications, cleanup).

plan.description:
Plan (list of steps) executed by the job.

Each item is a step object. Typical steps are get/put/task and grouping steps like in_parallel/do/try.

public.description: Whether job builds are publicly visible in the UI (depends on auth).

serial.description:
If true, run only one build of this job at a time.

Use for deployments or any job that must not overlap with itself.

serial_groups.description:
Serial groups for shared serialization across jobs.

Jobs that share a serial group will not run concurrently (useful for multiple deploy jobs targeting the same environment).

max_in_flight.description:
Maximum number of builds of this job that may run concurrently.

Use this when the job *can* overlap but you want an upper bound (e.g. expensive test jobs).

If you want strictly one-at-a-time, prefer serial: true.

disable_manual_trigger.description:
If true, the job cannot be manually triggered from the UI/CLI (only automatic triggers apply).

Useful to prevent accidental deployments.

interruptible.description:
If true, running builds of this job may be interrupted when a newer build is triggered.

Useful for jobs where only the latest result matters (e.g. long-running tests on frequently updated branches).

build_log_retention.description:
Build log retention policy.

This is a structured object whose shape depends on Concourse version. It controls how many builds/logs are kept.

stepHook.description:
Hook step executed depending on outcome.

Shape: { do: [ <steps...> ] }.

Use hooks for notifications (e.g. put: slack) and cleanup tasks.

do.description: Steps to execute as the hook body.

step.description:
A single plan step.

Most steps are objects with a step-type key (get/put/task/in_parallel/do/try/set_pipeline/load_var/across).

Additionally, Concourse supports wrapper keys like timeout/attempts/tags that modify an inner step.

Rule of thumb: exactly one primary type key should be present in the object.

setPipelineStep.description:
set_pipeline step: Create/update another pipeline from within a job.

Common use cases:
- One pipeline manages another (bootstrapping)
- Dynamic pipelines based on repo contents

Typical usage:
- set_pipeline: my-pipeline
  file: repo/ci/pipeline.yml
  vars: { some: var }
  var_files: [repo/ci/vars.yml]

Note: The exact keys/behavior can vary by Concourse version; this schema covers the common shape.

file.description: Path to the pipeline YAML file (usually inside an input fetched via get).

vars.description: Inline variables for interpolating the pipeline definition.

var_files.description: List of variable files to interpolate into the pipeline definition.

instance_vars.description: Instance vars for instanced pipelines (if used).

loadVarStep.description:
load_var step: Load a variable value from a file into build-local vars.

Use this to read generated data (JSON/YAML/raw) from the workspace and then reference it later in the plan via ((.:varname)) or similar Concourse syntax (version-dependent).

Typical usage:
- load_var: version
  file: repo/version.txt
  format: raw

format controls parsing (raw/json/yaml).

load_var.description: Name of the var to load.

format.description: Parsing format for the file contents.

reveal.description: If true, the loaded value may be shown in build output (use carefully with secrets).

acrossStep.description:
across step: Matrix/iteration functionality (advanced).

This lets you run a step multiple times across a set of values (like a build matrix).

Because across is advanced and has multiple shapes depending on Concourse version, this schema only documents the concept and keeps the structure permissive.

do.description: Steps to execute for each combination.

fail_fast.description: If true, stop other iterations when one fails.

timeoutStep.description:
timeout wrapper: Apply a timeout to an inner step.

Typical usage:
- timeout: 10m
  do:
    - task: slow-tests
      file: repo/ci/tasks/tests.yml

This schema models timeout as a wrapper with an inner step under 'do' or 'step'. Exact shapes vary; keep it simple.

attemptsStep.description:
attempts wrapper: Retry an inner step up to N times.

Typical usage:
- attempts: 3
  task: flaky
  file: repo/ci/tasks/flaky.yml

Use this for transient failures (network, flaky external systems). Avoid masking real failures.

tagsStep.description:
tags wrapper: Force an inner step to run on workers with specific tags.

Typical usage:
- tags: [linux, gpu]
  task: train
  file: repo/ci/tasks/train.yml

Useful for hardware/OS constraints.

getStep.description:
get step: Fetch a resource version into the build.

Typical usage:
- get: app-repo
  trigger: true

Common options:
- trigger: run the job when a new version appears
- passed: constrain versions to those produced by other jobs
- params: resource-type specific parameters
- version: pin to a specific version or use selectors (e.g. every)

get.description: Resource name to fetch (must match an entry in top-level resources).

trigger.description: If true, a new resource version triggers a new build of the job.

passed.description: Version constraint: only use versions that have passed the given job(s).

params.description: Resource-type specific parameters for the get.

version.description: Version selector. Often a string like 'every' or an object understood by the resource type.

putStep.description:
put step: Update a resource (publish something).

Typical usage:
- put: image
  params: { image: build/image.tar }

Common options:
- params: resource-type specific parameters
- get_params: control the implicit get after put
- inputs: which inputs to pass into the put container
- timeout/tags: execution controls

put.description: Resource name to update (must match top-level resources).

params.description: Resource-type specific parameters for the put (what to publish).

get_params.description: Params used for the implicit get after put (resource-type specific).

inputs.description:
Which inputs to pass to the put step. Options:
- all: pass all inputs
- detect: only pass inputs referenced by params
- explicit list: pass only these input names

taskStep.description:
task step: Run a task (a script/program inside a container).

Two ways to define the task:
- file: point to a task.yml inside an input
- config: inline the task config

Common fields:
- params: env vars for the task
- vars: interpolation vars for the task file
- input_mapping/output_mapping: rename inputs/outputs
- privileged: allow privileged mode (use sparingly)

file.description: Path to a task definition file inside an input (e.g. 'repo/ci/tasks/unit.yml').

image.description: Shorthand to select an image resource (advanced/optional).

privileged.description: Run task in privileged container. Use only if required.

inParallelStep.description:
in_parallel step: Run steps in parallel.

You can provide either:
- a list of steps
- or an object with { steps, limit, fail_fast }

Use this to speed up independent work (e.g. run lint + tests at the same time).

limit.description: Max parallelism. If omitted, Concourse decides.

fail_fast.description: If true, fail fast on first failure.

doStep.description:
do step: Run a list of steps in sequence as a group.

Use this to group steps together (also useful inside hooks or try).

tryStep.description:
try step: Try a step; failure does not fail the build.

Use this for optional steps (e.g. best-effort notifications).
